1. Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially when recent history shows rising prices.  
2. Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., post-85+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to reflect mean reversion.  
3. Forecast mean is too low relative to true mean, especially in high-volatility periods — adjust upward by 1–3% of the historical mean.  
4. Model lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends — shift forecast up by 1–2% for the first 3 days.  
5. When true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day avg), model fails to capture it — increase forecast by 2–5% of the recent 7-day average.  
6. Model underreacts to low-price periods — if true outcome drops below 70% of prior 30-day average, increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid underestimation.  
7. Avoid forecasting below 70% of the 30-day historical mean unless confirmed by strong downward trend signals.  
8. If model forecast is >10% below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, adjust upward by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
9. In high volatility periods, reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to avoid over-optimistic spikes.  
10. Always check for “mean reversion bias” — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until alignment.
